title: Anharmonic dephasing in the electron-phonon interaction
abstract: Electron-phonon coupling has been a central topic in condensed matter physics for decades, and firstprinciples methods have demonstrated remarkable success in quantitatively capturing its role in a wide variety of physical phenomena and materials. Conventional calculations of electron-phonon coupling typically assume that phonons have infinite lifetimes, but phonons can exhibit finite lifetimes due to anharmonic phonon-phonon interactions. In this work, we derive an expression for the electron-phonon coupling scattering rates including the effects of anharmonic three-phonon interactions, which lead to phonon dephasing and finite phonon lifetimes. We also describe a first-principles implementation of this anharmonic electron-phonon coupling which can be seamlessly integrated within existing workflows for the evaluation of electron-phonon and phonon-phonon coupling interactions. Finally, we present calculations of electron-phonon scattering rates including phonon dephasing in a range of materials, and discuss the different microscopic mechanisms by which anharmonic phonons influence electron-phonon coupling. This study establishes the importance of finite phonon lifetimes in the evaluation of electron-phonon coupling, and provides a platform to explore these effects in a wide range of materials and phenomena.
summary: This work develops a theoretical framework to calculate electron-phonon scattering rates by explicitly including phonon dephasing caused by anharmonic lattice vibrations. By extending standard many-body perturbation theory, the authors show that finite phonon lifetimes significantly impact electronic transport properties in materials like Si and PbTe.
main_problem: The primary goal is to accurately calculate electron-phonon coupling scattering rates by incorporating the effects of finite phonon lifetimes arising from anharmonic three-phonon interactions.
main_result: The study derives a new expression for these scattering rates and establishes that accounting for finite phonon lifetimes is crucial for an accurate evaluation of electron-phonon coupling in various materials.
method: The authors use advanced many-body perturbation theory, extending standard self-energy calculations (like Fan-Migdal) to include anharmonic corrections via three-phonon diagrams.
model_or_system: The system is the electron-phonon interaction within crystalline solids (e.g., Si, PbTe). The theoretical framework involves coupling Hamiltonians ($\hat{H}_0 + \hat{V}_{ep} + \hat{V}_{pp}$) and calculating self-energies using Matsubara Green's functions.
key_observables: Electron-phonon scattering rates, electronic state lifetimes (imaginary part of the electron self-energy), and phonon spectral function renormalization.
important_parameters: The relative timescales between phonon-phonon interaction ($	au_{ph-ph}$) and electron-phonon interaction ($	au_{e-ph}$); temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: Conventional calculations often assume $	au_{ph-ph} \gg 	au_{e-ph}$, which the work aims to correct for when timescales become comparable.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Feynman diagrams (Fan-Migdal, Debye-Waller) and show convergence plots of calculated scattering rates as computational grid sizes increase for materials like PbTe.
paper_structure: The paper systematically builds the theory: first establishing the Hamiltonian, then deriving the standard electron self-energy ($\Sigma_{FM}$), followed by incorporating the phonon self-energy ($\Pi$) from anharmonic interactions, and finally presenting calculations of scattering rates using these combined effects.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the treatment of finite lifetimes and complex many-body self-energies shares mathematical parallels with open quantum system dynamics where environmental coupling (like phonons) leads to decoherence and energy renormalization.
